provenance.operatorDescription: Routes the one subscription that covers the hearing's court house through each of SubscriptionsService.getSubscriptions's OTHER four match arms.
provenance.operatorRationale: Defect rows C4, C5 and C30 are all statements about which arm of SubscriptionsService.getSubscriptions (lines 15-42) a court-register subscription is allowed to match through, and the real 274-entry capture exercises exactly one of them: every one of its 133 court-register subscriptions matches on `selectedCourtHouses` and nothing else. No entry carries an `informantCode` (40 non-register entries do), none is flagged `isPrisonCourtRegisterSubscription` (3 non-register entries are), none is also a NOWs subscription, and no entry anywhere sets `anyMajorCreditor`. So the corpus recorded the three rows' subject matter not at all, and the audit found them explaining nothing. This operator takes the Wandsworth YOT entry — the ONE entry whose selectedCourtHouses covers B01LY00 — closes the court-house route it currently matches by, and re-opens it through each accidental route in turn. On the legacy every one of them matches and a register is produced; the port matches none of them, so the register is not produced, and THAT is the difference the three rows claim. The two major-creditor variants keep the court-house route open and vary the flag instead, because C30 is about a vocabulary answer and not about a route: `anyMajorCreditor` passes vacuously on empty data while `prosecutorMajorCreditor` cannot pass on the same empty data, which is the asymmetry the row is about and which the pair measures rather than asserts.
